title: Linking verbs: be, appear, seem; become, get
summary: Глаголы-связки (be, seem, appear, become, get, go, turn, fall, look, sound, feel...) — после них идёт прилагательное, а не наречие; тонкости seem/appear и выбор между become, get и другими глаголами перемены.
ru:
## Что такое глагол-связка
Связочный глагол не обозначает действие, а **соединяет подлежащее с его описанием**: прилагательным или существительным. Главные связки — **be, seem, appear, become, get, remain, stay, look, sound, feel, taste, smell, turn, grow, go, prove**. После них нужно **прилагательное**, а не наречие.
> The plan sounds **reasonable**. — План звучит разумно.
> The soup tastes **awful**. — Суп на вкус ужасный.
- ~~She looked happily.~~ → She looked **happy**.
- ~~The engine sounds strangely.~~ → The engine sounds **strange**.
Эти же глаголы бывают и обычными, тогда после них наречие: She looked **carefully** at the map (она смотрела — действие). Проверка: можно ли заменить глагол на **be**? Если да — это связка: *He looks tired* = He is tired.

## seem и appear
**seem** нейтрален, **appear** звучит формальнее и чаще встречается в письменной речи и новостях. Оба описывают впечатление, а не факт. Возможные модели:
- + прилагательное: The results **seem inconsistent**.
- + to-infinitive: She **seems to know** everyone. / He **appears to have left** (раньше) / They **seem to be arguing** (сейчас).
- **It seems / appears (that)** + предложение: It seems that nobody noticed the error.
- **seem like / as if / as though**: It seems like a good idea. (like + существительное — нейтрально; like + целое предложение, *It seems like we're lost*, — разговорно) / It seems **as if** we're lost.
- **There seems / appears to be**: There seems to be a mistake in the invoice. Глагол согласуется с существительным: There **seem** to be several problems.
- Отрицание обычно при глаголе: He **doesn't seem to** like it. Форма *seems not to like* — формальная и редкая.
- **can't seem to** = «никак не получается»: I can't seem to focus today.
**seem** не употребляется в Continuous: ~~She is seeming tired.~~ → She **seems** tired. А вот **appear** в значении «появляться, выступать» — обычный глагол: The singer is appearing in Vienna this week.

## become и get
Оба значат «становиться», но стиль и сочетаемость разные.
- **become** — нейтрально/формально; после него и **прилагательное**, и **существительное**: She became a surgeon. / The weather became increasingly unstable.
- **get** — разговорно; только **прилагательное или причастие**: get tired, get better, get lost, get engaged, get used to. Постепенное изменение: It's **getting** harder and harder to find a flat.
> He **became** a minister at 35. — Он стал министром в 35 лет. (~~He got a minister.~~ — это было бы «получил министра»)
> I'm **getting** hungry. — Я уже начинаю хотеть есть.

## Другие глаголы перемены — устойчивые сочетания
Здесь выбор глагола задан сочетанием, его надо запоминать:
- **go** — обычно к худшему: go wrong, go bad, go mad, go bankrupt, go blind, go grey.
- **turn** — резкая смена, цвета: turn red, turn nasty, turn sour, turn professional.
- **grow** — постепенно, книжно: grow old, grow tired, grow louder.
- **fall**: fall ill, fall asleep, fall silent, fall in love. **come**: come true, come undone. **run**: run dry, run short.
- Сохранение состояния: **remain, stay, keep** (keep calm, stay silent, remain unclear); **prove** = оказываться: The method proved effective.
- ~~go ill~~ → **fall** ill; ~~become asleep~~ → **fall** asleep.

## Чувства: look, sound, feel, taste, smell
После них — прилагательное; если хотим сравнить с существительным, нужен **like**; если с целым предложением — **as if / as though**.
> It smells **wonderful**. / It smells **like** fresh bread. / It smells **as if** someone has been baking.
> I feel **terrible**. — Мне плохо. (~~I feel terribly.~~) Для здоровья: I don't feel **well**.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~She seems to be knowing the answer.~~ → She seems **to know** the answer.
- ~~It seems that he not likes it.~~ → It seems that he **doesn't like** it.
- ~~He became ill and got the head of the department.~~ → …and **became** the head.
- The leaves became red. — допустимо, но естественнее: The leaves **turned** red.
en:
## Linking verbs
A linking verb does not describe an action. It connects the subject with a description: an adjective or a noun. The main ones are **be, seem, appear, become, get, remain, stay, look, sound, feel, taste, smell, turn, grow, go, prove**. After them we use an **adjective**, not an adverb.
> The plan sounds **reasonable**.
> The soup tastes **awful**.
- ~~She looked happily.~~ → She looked **happy**.
The same verbs can be ordinary action verbs, and then an adverb follows: She looked **carefully** at the map. Test: if you can replace the verb with **be**, it is a linking verb.

## seem and appear
**seem** is neutral; **appear** is more formal and typical of writing and news. Both describe an impression, not a proven fact.
- + adjective: The results **seem inconsistent**.
- + to-infinitive: She **seems to know** everyone. / He **appears to have left**. / They **seem to be arguing**.
- **It seems / appears (that)** + clause: It seems that nobody noticed.
- **seem like / as if / as though**: It seems **as if** we are lost.
- **There seems / appears to be**: There seem to be several problems (the verb agrees with the noun).
- Negatives: He **doesn't seem to** like it. (*seems not to* is rare and formal.)
- **can't seem to**: I can't seem to concentrate today.
**seem** is not used in continuous forms: ~~She is seeming tired.~~ The verb **appear** meaning «to perform» or «to come into view» is a normal verb.

## become and get
Both mean «change into a new state».
- **become**: neutral or formal; followed by an adjective **or a noun**: She became a surgeon.
- **get**: informal; adjective or participle only: get tired, get lost, get used to. Good for gradual change: It's **getting** harder to find a flat.

## Other verbs of change are collocations
- **go**: usually negative: go wrong, go bad, go mad, go bankrupt, go blind.
- **turn**: sudden or colour change: turn red, turn sour, turn nasty.
- **grow**: gradual, a little literary: grow old, grow tired.
- **fall**: fall ill, fall asleep, fall silent. **come**: come true. **run**: run dry.
- Staying the same: **remain, stay, keep**. **prove** = turn out: The method proved effective.

## The senses
Use an adjective after **look, sound, feel, taste, smell**; **like** before a noun; **as if** before a clause.
> It smells **wonderful**. / It smells **like** fresh bread. / It smells **as if** someone has been baking.

## Common mistakes
- ~~She seems to be knowing the answer.~~ → She seems **to know** the answer.
- ~~go ill~~ → **fall** ill.
- ~~I feel terribly.~~ → I feel **terrible**.
structure:
## Модели с seem / appear
| Модель | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| seem / appear + adjective | впечатление о состоянии | The offer seems generous. |
| seem / appear + to + infinitive | то же время | He seems to enjoy it. |
| seem / appear + to be + -ing | процесс сейчас | They appear to be negotiating. |
| seem / appear + to have + V3 | раньше | She seems to have forgotten. |
| It seems / appears (that) + clause | общее впечатление | It seems that nobody called. |
| There seems / appears to be + noun | существование | There seems to be a delay. |
| seem like / as if + ... | сравнение | It seems as if it will rain. |

## become / get / go / turn / grow / fall
| Глагол | Оттенок | Примеры |
|---|---|---|
| become | нейтрально; adj. и noun | become a manager; become aware |
| get | разговорно; adj. / V3 | get tired; get lost; get better |
| go | обычно к худшему | go wrong; go bad; go blind |
| turn | резкая смена, цвет | turn red; turn sour |
| grow | постепенно | grow old; grow louder |
| fall | вход в состояние | fall ill; fall asleep |
| come / run | устойчиво | come true; run dry |

## Формула
> subject + linking verb + **adjective** (not adverb)
> It sounds **great**. ~~It sounds greatly.~~
> subject + look / sound / feel + **like** + noun; + **as if** + clause

exercises.title: Прилагательное или наречие?
exercises.instruction: Выберите нужную форму из пары в подсказке и впишите её.
exercises.example: She looked (angry / angrily) at the clock. → She looked **angrily** at the clock (действие); She looked **angry** (состояние).

items.text: The engine sounded {{terrible}}, so we pulled over.
She looked {{carefully}} at every page of the contract.
After the long flight he felt {{dizzy}}.
The fish smells {{fresh}}, so I'll buy it.
The audience grew {{restless}} as the speech dragged on.
He remained {{silent}} throughout the whole meeting.
The proposal appeared {{reasonable}} at first sight.

exercises.title: Глаголы перемены состояния
exercises.instruction: Поставьте глагол из подсказки в нужную форму (go, turn, grow, fall, come, run, remain).

items.text: The children {{fell}} asleep in the car before we left the city.
By the end of the summer the river had {{run}} dry.
Her dream finally {{came}} true when she won the scholarship.
Everything started to {{go}} wrong after the merger.
As he {{grew}} older, he became more patient.
The cause of the accident {{remains|remained}} unclear.

items.q: She ___ to be having trouble with the new software.
items.why: **seem** не употребляется в Continuous; длительность передаёт инфинитив: seems **to be having**.

items.q: There ___ to be several mistakes in the report.
items.why: После there глагол согласуется с существительным: several mistakes → **seem**.

items.q: He doesn't ___ to understand how serious the situation is.
It ___ as if nobody had read the instructions.
items.why: Модель **It seemed as if + clause**; to-infinitive здесь невозможен, Continuous тоже.

items.q: The suspect ___ to have left the country before the police arrived.
items.why: Действие произошло раньше → **appears to have left**; Continuous в этом значении не нужен.

items.q: That ___ like a reasonable offer to me.
items.why: **sound like + noun**; Continuous с глаголами восприятия впечатления не используется.

exercises.title: become, get, go, fall
exercises.instruction: Выберите глагол, который сочетается с данным словом.

items.q: After years of work she ___ a leading expert in her field.
items.why: Перед существительным (expert) нужен **become**; get — только с прилагательным.
Разговорное постепенное изменение — **get**: устойчивое it's getting late («уже поздно»). Обратите внимание: ~~we're getting late~~ — так не говорят.

items.q: Something has ___ wrong with the printer.
Jack ___ ill on the flight and had to see a doctor.
It took me months to ___ used to the climate.
My grandfather ___ blind in his seventies.
items.why: **go blind** — стандартное сочетание для потери зрения; fall/turn здесь не подходят.

exercises.title: Перефразируйте с seem / appear
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, начиная со слов после стрелки, и сохраните смысл. Можно использовать seem или appear.

items.prompt: It seems that the manager has resigned. → The manager ...
answers: The manager seems to have resigned.
The manager appears to have resigned.

items.prompt: It appears that they are negotiating a deal. → They ...
answers: They appear to be negotiating a deal.
They seem to be negotiating a deal.

items.prompt: It seems that there is a problem with the engine. → There ...
answers: There seems to be a problem with the engine.
There appears to be a problem with the engine.

items.prompt: It seems that she doesn't enjoy her job. → She ...
answers: She doesn't seem to enjoy her job.
She does not seem to enjoy her job.
She doesn't appear to enjoy her job.
She does not appear to enjoy her job.
She seems not to enjoy her job.
She appears not to enjoy her job.

items.prompt: It seems that our flight was cancelled. → Our flight ...
answers: Our flight seems to have been cancelled.
Our flight appears to have been cancelled.
Our flight seems to have been canceled.
Our flight appears to have been canceled.

items.prompt: It appears that prices are rising. → Prices ...
answers: Prices appear to be rising.
Prices seem to be rising.
It's getting dark.
It is getting dark.
This idea sounds wonderful.
That idea sounds wonderful.
The idea sounds wonderful.
He doesn't seem to know the answer.
He does not seem to know the answer.
He seems not to know the answer.
The milk has gone sour.
The milk's gone sour.
The milk went sour.

items.prompt: Она заснула на диване. (she / fall / asleep / on the sofa)
answers: She fell asleep on the sofa.
The situation remains unclear.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя связки из юнита.

items.prompt: Опишите, как звучит или выглядит ваш любимый город (sound / look / feel).
items.sample: My home town looks beautiful in autumn, and it sounds quiet in the evening.

items.prompt: Что в вашей работе или учёбе стало труднее в последнее время? (get)
items.sample: Studying has got harder because the texts are getting longer.

items.prompt: Назовите случай, когда что-то пошло не так (go wrong).
items.sample: Last week my presentation went wrong because the projector broke.

items.prompt: Чем вы стали или хотите стать профессионально? (become)
items.sample: I want to become a translator one day.

items.prompt: Расскажите о чём-то, что кажется вам странным в последнее время (seem / appear).
items.sample: It seems that fewer people read paper books these days.

items.prompt: Опишите вкус или запах вашего любимого блюда (taste / smell).
items.sample: My mother's soup smells wonderful and tastes even better.
